candidate_relations.reason: FTD-ALS is a standard clinical equivalent of FTLD-MND, and the TBK1 etiology is supported by the pathogenic p.E643del variant.
ALS captures the motor neuron disease component but omits the required frontotemporal cognitive/degenerative component.
ALS-FTD spectrum disorder corresponds to FTLD-MND, with TBK1 etiology supported by genetic testing.
This states both required components of FTLD-MND and correctly identifies the documented TBK1 cause.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Concurrent ALS and FTD due to TBK1

candidate_relations.reason: FTDP-17 is a different diagnostic entity, classically linked to chromosome 17 genes such as MAPT or GRN, and does not specify the required MND composite.
ALS-FTD is a standard clinical synonym for the FTLD-MND diagnostic spectrum.
TBK1-associated FTD captures the cognitive/FTLD component and etiology but omits the required motor neuron disease component.
It replaces the required motor neuron disease component with parkinsonism; dopaminergic imaging abnormalities do not make this composite equivalent to FTLD-MND.
The wording 'and/or' permits isolated FTD or isolated ALS and therefore does not fully assert the benchmark's combined FTLD-MND object.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Broad FTD/ALS umbrella without requiring both components

candidate_relations.reason: This is an etiologically specified equivalent of FTLD-MND and is supported by the pathogenic TBK1 variant.
ALS-FTD spectrum disorder corresponds to FTLD-MND, with the stated TBK1 relationship supported by testing.
Vertical gaze palsy can suggest progressive supranuclear palsy, but PSP does not account for the benchmark FTLD-MND composite and documented bulbar motor neuron findings.
The label includes both the frontotemporal and motor neuron disease components and the documented TBK1 etiology.
This is a standard equivalent formulation of FTLD-MND with the supported genetic etiology retained.
